title: 2027 Nissan Frontier: $15 Cheaper Than a Tacoma, But There Is a Catch

scenes.text: The Nissan Frontier is up almost forty percent this year, and for twenty twenty-seven, its cheapest crew cab costs fifteen dollars less than a Toyota Tacoma. Fifteen dollars. But the Frontier has a weakness that the sales numbers do not show, and it is the one number that most buyers never check. Here is what changed on the twenty twenty-seven Nissan Frontier, and whether it is worth buying.
scenes.caption: 2027 NISSAN FRONTIER: WORTH IT?

scenes.text: Nissan is the company that ended its full-size Titan after the twenty twenty-four model year. Motor Authority reported it in August of twenty twenty-three, and the Titan sold just thirteen trucks through nine months of twenty twenty-six. But the Frontier, the midsize truck, tells a different story. Nissan sold sixty-six thousand, five hundred thirteen Frontiers through nine months, up thirty-nine point six percent from forty-seven thousand, six hundred thirty.
scenes.caption: FRONTIER: 66,513 (+39.6%)

scenes.text: The quarters are consistent. In the first half, sales rose almost forty-one percent, to forty-three thousand, one hundred one. In the second quarter, thirty-four point six percent. In the third quarter, thirty-seven and a half percent, to twenty-three thousand, four hundred twelve. This is not a one-quarter spike. It is a steady, large gain, and it has made the Frontier the fastest-growing truck in our ranking of the ten best sellers.
scenes.caption: Q2: +34.6%. Q3: +37.5%.

scenes.text: For the twenty twenty-seven details, we used Nissan's own pricing release from June fifteenth, Autoblog's report from June sixteenth, and Kelley Blue Book's headline. For sales, Pickup Truck Talk and The Fast Lane Truck. For resale, iSeeCars. Where two sources disagree, we say so. Every source is listed in the description, and prices are the manufacturer's suggested prices, not what you will pay.
scenes.query: Nissan Frontier S King Cab pickup
scenes.caption: SOURCES: NISSAN, AUTOBLOG, KBB, ISEECARS

scenes.text: There is a twist in each part of this story. One engine explains the sales. One price comparison is almost a tie. One resale number is the lowest in its class. And one study puts the Frontier below the truck average. Stay with me, because the last twist is about the truck that is outselling the Frontier more than three to one.
scenes.caption: FOUR TWISTS

scenes.text: Change number one is the price. According to Nissan, the twenty twenty-seven Frontier starts at thirty-two thousand, four hundred ninety dollars, for the S King Cab with two-wheel drive. Autoblog reports that every trim rose by between three hundred and three hundred forty dollars compared with twenty twenty-six. The S King Cab with four-wheel drive is thirty-five thousand, four hundred ninety, and the cheapest crew cab, the S two-wheel drive, is thirty-three thousand, eight hundred ninety.
scenes.query: Nissan Frontier S Crew Cab pickup
scenes.caption: 2027 FRONTIER: FROM $32,490

scenes.text: The rest of the range goes up quickly. The SV crew cab with two-wheel drive and a five foot bed is thirty-six thousand, four hundred ninety. The PRO-X is thirty-eight thousand, eight hundred ninety. The SV crew cab four-wheel drive is thirty-nine thousand, seven hundred ninety, and the PRO-4X, the off-road version, is forty-two thousand, one hundred ninety, or forty-two thousand, six hundred ninety with the six foot bed.
scenes.caption: PRO-4X: $42,190 TO $42,690

scenes.text: The twist is the destination fee. Nissan's release lists one thousand, seven hundred seventy-five dollars. Autoblog says the fee rises from sixteen ninety-five to seventeen forty-five. Kelley Blue Book's headline says the Frontier starts at thirty-four thousand, two hundred thirty-five, which is thirty-two thousand, four hundred ninety plus seventeen forty-five. So the sources disagree by thirty dollars on the fee. The real price is the sticker plus the fee, and you should ask for the exact number.
scenes.caption: DESTINATION FEE: $1,745 OR $1,775?

scenes.text: Change number two is the comparison with the Toyota Tacoma. According to Autoblog, the cheapest Frontier crew cab, the S two-wheel drive with the five foot bed, costs thirty-three thousand, eight hundred ninety. The closest Tacoma, the twenty twenty-six SR Double Cab short bed two-wheel drive, costs thirty-three thousand, nine hundred five. So the Frontier is fifteen dollars cheaper. Autoblog notes that Toyota had not yet released twenty twenty-seven Tacoma prices.
scenes.query: Toyota Tacoma SR Double Cab pickup
scenes.caption: FRONTIER $33,890. TACOMA $33,905.

scenes.text: That is almost a tie on price, and it means the price is not what separates the two trucks. What separates them is what you get for the money. The Frontier has a three point eight liter V six with three hundred ten horsepower, a nine-speed automatic, and tows up to seven thousand, one hundred fifty pounds. The Tacoma starts with a two point four liter turbo four-cylinder, and has a hybrid with three hundred twenty-six horsepower.
scenes.caption: FRONTIER: V6, 310 HP, 7,150 LB

scenes.text: And here is the twist about the sales. At nearly the same price, the Tacoma sold two hundred fourteen thousand, eight hundred seventy-five through nine months, and the Frontier sixty-six thousand, five hundred thirteen. That is more than three times as many. The Frontier is growing faster, up forty percent against five percent for the Tacoma. But a company growing from a smaller base can grow a lot and still be far behind.
scenes.caption: TACOMA OUTSELLS FRONTIER 3.2 TO 1

scenes.text: Number three is the engine, which is the reason people give for buying the Frontier. The Fast Lane Truck credited Nissan's naturally aspirated V six, and said buyers seem to be listening. Autoblog's list of the cheapest trucks describes it as the only naturally aspirated V six on the list, and says it has heavier steering. SlashGear says Road and Track called the Frontier a blast from the past, and notes that it includes a twelve point three inch touchscreen.
scenes.caption: THE ONLY NATURALLY ASPIRATED V6

scenes.text: Here is the twist. The engine is unchanged for twenty twenty-seven, according to Autoblog, still three hundred ten horsepower and two hundred eighty-one pound-feet of torque. The Tacoma's hybrid makes three hundred twenty-six horsepower and four hundred sixty-five pound-feet, which is much more torque. So the Frontier's V six is not about power. It is about simplicity. A truck with no turbo and no hybrid system has fewer parts to fail, and buyers seem to value that.
scenes.caption: FRONTIER: 281 LB-FT. TACOMA HYBRID: 465.

scenes.text: The V six is built at Nissan's plant in Decherd, Tennessee, according to Nissan's release. That is a detail worth knowing, because the cost of tariffs depends in part on where parts are made. We do not have a source that tells us how much that affects the Frontier's price. But the fact that the price rose by only about three hundred dollars, while many trucks rose by thousands, is consistent with a company that is trying to hold on to the buyers it has won.
scenes.caption: ENGINE BUILT IN DECHERD, TENNESSEE

scenes.text: Change number four is what is new for twenty twenty-seven, and it is small. There is a new Sport Edition package, nine hundred ninety dollars, for the SV trim, with black lower front fascia, grille and mirrors, black seventeen-inch wheels with all-terrain tires, an aluminum skid plate, LED fog lights and yellow stitching inside. There is a moonroof on the PRO-X and the PRO-4X, a new Alpine Metallic paint, and a Qi two wireless charger.
scenes.caption: NEW: SPORT EDITION ($990)

scenes.text: The twist is that nothing mechanical changed. Same engine, same transmission, same towing. Nissan is selling the same truck with a new package and a small price increase. And that is a reasonable strategy when sales are up almost forty percent. A company does not usually reinvent a truck that is working. The risk is that the competition, with a hybrid Tacoma and a hybrid Maverick, keeps moving.
scenes.caption: SAME TRUCK. NEW PACKAGE.

scenes.text: Now the weakness we promised. According to iSeeCars, the Frontier keeps sixty-three point four percent of its value after five years, the lowest of the five midsize trucks on the list. The Tacoma keeps eighty and a half, the Ranger sixty-eight point eight, the Canyon sixty-six point eight and the Gladiator sixty-five point two. So the Frontier is last of five.
scenes.caption: FRONTIER RESALE: 63.4%, LAST OF 5

scenes.text: And in the longevity study, the picture is the same. In the earlier edition we could read, the Frontier had a twelve and a half percent chance of reaching two hundred fifty thousand miles, when the truck average was twenty-five point nine percent. That is about half the average. In the newest edition, it is not among the top twelve trucks. The Tacoma, in the same studies, is fourth in both editions. So the Frontier sells well, and does not do as well on holding up.
scenes.caption: LONGEVITY: 12.5% VS 25.9% AVERAGE

scenes.text: Let's put that in dollars, as an example. Take the cheapest Frontier crew cab, at thirty-three thousand, eight hundred ninety dollars. At sixty-three point four percent resale, it would be worth about twenty-one thousand, four hundred eighty-six after five years, a loss of twelve thousand, four hundred four. The Tacoma at thirty-three thousand, nine hundred five, at eighty and a half percent, would be worth twenty-seven thousand, two hundred ninety-four, a loss of six thousand, six hundred eleven.
scenes.caption: FRONTIER LOSES ~$12,404. TACOMA ~$6,611.

scenes.text: That is a difference of about five thousand, eight hundred eight dollars in value, on trucks that cost almost the same on the day you buy. It is an estimate, using the cheapest crew cab prices and the averages from the study. But it shows what the price comparison hides. The Frontier is the cheaper truck by fifteen dollars, and may be the more expensive one to own.
scenes.caption: ~$5,808 GAP IN VALUE

scenes.text: Let's look at how the price climbs, because that is where many buyers get surprised. The cheapest Frontier is thirty-two thousand, four hundred ninety dollars, and the most expensive, the PRO-4X with the six foot bed, is forty-two thousand, six hundred ninety. That is a ladder of ten thousand, two hundred dollars. And the first big step on that ladder is four-wheel drive, which adds three thousand dollars on the S trims, and about three thousand, three hundred on the SV and the PRO.
scenes.caption: THE LADDER: $32,490 TO $42,690

scenes.text: The twist is what that does to the Tacoma comparison. The fifteen dollar gap is for the cheapest crew cab with two-wheel drive. But many buyers who want a midsize truck also want four-wheel drive, and the four-wheel drive Frontier S crew cab is thirty-six thousand, eight hundred ninety. We do not have a matching Tacoma price in the sources we used. So the honest answer is that the headline comparison applies to one trim only.
scenes.query: Nissan Frontier S Crew Cab 4x4 pickup
scenes.caption: 4X4 ADDS ABOUT $3,000

scenes.text: Next, the comparison with the other cheap trucks, from the Autoblog list. The Ford Maverick, twenty-eight thousand, one hundred forty-five. The Tacoma SR XtraCab, thirty-two thousand, one hundred forty-five. The Chevrolet Colorado work truck, thirty-two thousand, four hundred. The Ford Ranger XL, thirty-three thousand, three hundred fifty. And the twenty twenty-seven Frontier S King Cab, thirty-two thousand, four hundred ninety. The Frontier sits right in the middle of the pack.
scenes.caption: FRONTIER IN THE MIDDLE OF THE PACK

scenes.text: That middle position matters, because the buyer has real choices. For about thirty-two to thirty-three thousand dollars, you can choose a Tacoma with the best resale, a Colorado with a turbo and the most towing, a Ranger with a ten-speed, or a Frontier with a V six. Each one has a different strength. The Frontier's is simplicity and a growing following. The others have stronger numbers on resale and longevity.
scenes.caption: FOUR TRUCKS WITHIN $1,200

scenes.text: Now think about Nissan as a company. Through nine months, the Titan and the Frontier together sold sixty-six thousand, five hundred twenty-six trucks, up thirty-four percent. In our calculation from the Pickup Truck Talk table, Nissan went from about two point one percent of the trucks in that table to about two point nine percent. A gain of eight tenths of a point, in a flat market, is a large move for a small player.
scenes.caption: NISSAN SHARE: 2.1% TO 2.9%

scenes.text: And the Titan is the other half of that story. It sold two thousand and twenty-four trucks through nine months of twenty twenty-five, and thirteen in twenty twenty-six. Nissan did not close the Canton plant when it ended the Titan. According to Motor Authority at the time, the company said no job losses were planned, and that the plant would be retooled for electric vehicles. So Nissan made a choice, to leave the big truck market and to put its truck effort into the Frontier.
scenes.caption: TITAN: 2,024 TO 13

scenes.text: Whether that choice is right will take years to see. A midsize truck can grow quickly, but it is a smaller market than the full-size trucks, which sold more than one point six million through nine months. The Frontier's gain of nearly nineteen thousand trucks is real. But it equals only about one percent of the number of full-size trucks sold. A company that wants to be a major truck maker needs a bigger truck than this one.
scenes.caption: GROWTH IS REAL, MARKET IS SMALLER

scenes.text: The last twist is about who should buy the Frontier anyway. A buyer who wants a simple, naturally aspirated V six, a truck that tows over seven thousand pounds, and a price in the low thirties, has a good reason. A buyer who plans to keep the truck for ten years or more, and not worry about resale, can also decide that the lower resale does not matter. The numbers are about the market, not about your use.
scenes.caption: WHO SHOULD STILL BUY IT

scenes.text: And a buyer who plans to sell in five years should compare carefully. Ask the dealer for the out-the-door price, with the destination fee. Ask for the price of the Tacoma, the Colorado and the Ranger at the same time. And use the fifteen dollar gap with the Tacoma as a reminder that you are not buying the cheapest truck. You are buying a truck at a price where the market gives you many choices.
scenes.caption: COMPARE OUT-THE-DOOR PRICES

scenes.text: So what should you check before you buy a midsize truck in twenty twenty-seven? First, the out-the-door price with the destination fee. Second, the engine and the towing for the exact trim. Third, the five-year resale value, which is where the Frontier is weakest. And fourth, whether the model is still being built. We put all of this into a checklist, the Twenty Twenty-Seven Truck Buyer's Guide. The link is in the description and in the pinned comment.
scenes.caption: CHECK 1, 2, 3 AND 4
